findings_addressed.oracle: struct.pack / f-string '{b:02X}' in _render_hex_rows produces uppercase two-digit hex per byte; b'\xaa' -> 'AA', b'\xbb' -> 'BB', b'\xcc' -> 'CC', b'\xdd' -> 'DD'. These tokens cannot appear in the static _html_header() output and are therefore independent evidence that _render_hex_rows executed with the actual payload.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/bridges/hex_editor.py _render_hex_rows, change `hex_str = f"{b:02X}"` to `hex_str = f"{b:02x}"` (lowercase) — the assertions `assert 'AA' in result` and `assert 'BB' in result` etc. will FAIL because the output will contain 'aa' and 'bb' instead.

notes: Finding G0157: The original test only checked '<!DOCTYPE html>' and '</html>', both of which come from the static _html_header() return value and the hardcoded closing line, making the test pass even if _render_hex_rows was a no-op. Added four assertions ('AA', 'BB', 'CC', 'DD') that correspond to the uppercase hex rendering of the injected payload bytes (\xaa\xbb\xcc\xdd). These tokens are produced exclusively by _render_hex_rows and cannot appear in the static header, so their presence constitutes an independent oracle proving the rendering path executed. The sibling test test_html_export_contains_hex_data also checks hex content but does NOT check DOCTYPE/closing tag structure; the two tests gate complementary behaviours and are not duplicates.
